title: Finiteness and radiciality of the scalar-extended scheme Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0$ has $q$ elements and $k$ is its fixed algebraic closure. Let $X_0$ be a $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let

$$
\Phi=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{X_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k:X\longrightarrow X
$$

be the scalar-extended $q$-power Frobenius of [def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber], whose affine ring map is $u\otimes b\mapsto u^q\otimes b$. Then $\Phi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and radicial [def-weil-radicial-morphism]. No separatedness or reducedness assumption is imposed on $X_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CCD, label lemma-relative-frobenius-finite; Tag 0CCB, label lemma-relative-frobenius; Tag 0CCG, label remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius. Apply to the a-fold relative Frobenius over k_0, whose q-power Frobenius is the identity, then extend scalars to k.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and let $f:X_0\to S$ be the structure map. Finite type implies locally finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The finite-field datum supplies a prime $p$ and $a\geq1$, and $X_0$ and $S$ have characteristic $p$ as in [def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber]. Applying [lem-trf-relative-frobenius-finite] with $n=a$ proves that $R_a=F_{X_0/S}^{(a)}:X_0\to X_0^{(p^a/S)}$ is finite.

Here is the radiciality argument, including the iteration identification. Set $Y_i=X_0\times_{S,F_S^i}S$ for $0\leq i\leq a$, with $Y_0=X_0$, and write $\pi_i:Y_i\to X_0$ for the first projection. Associating the fibre products gives $(Y_i)^{(p/S)}\cong Y_{i+1}$: the two successive base changes are along $F_S^i$ and $F_S$, whose composite is $F_S^{i+1}$; both directions of this identification are the unique maps with the given projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $r_i:Y_i\to Y_{i+1}$ be the one-step relative Frobenius under this identification. Each $r_i$ is a universal homeomorphism by [lem-trf-relative-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism], since every $Y_i$ is over the characteristic-$p$ scheme $S$. A homeomorphism is injective after each base change, so [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism, def-weil-radicial-morphism] imply that each $r_i$ is radicial. For clarity, the composite $C_i=r_{i-1}\circ\cdots\circ r_0:X_0\to Y_i$ has projection to $X_0$ equal to $F_{X_0}^i$ and projection to $S$ equal to $f$. This holds for $i=1$ by the definition of relative Frobenius; the induction step uses that the first projection of $r_i$ is $F_{Y_i}$ and that $\pi_iF_{Y_i}=F_{X_0}\pi_i$, an equality of structure-sheaf maps because homomorphisms preserve $p$th powers [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore identifies $C_a$ with $R_a$. Composition stability in [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] makes $R_a$ radicial. Now $c^q=c$ in $k_0$ by [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card], so $F_S^a=\operatorname{id}_S$. Thus $Y_a\cong X_0$, and the first projection of $R_a$ is $F_{X_0}^a=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{X_0}=\Phi_0$ by [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme, def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber]. Under this canonical identification the model map $\Phi_0$ is finite and radicial.

source.place: Tag 0CCB, lemma-relative-frobenius; Tag 0CCG, remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius, first factorization formula, with the projection check written out

proof.text: The morphism in the statement is $\Phi=\Phi_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k$, the base change of $\Phi_0$ along $k_0\to k$, by [def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber] and [def-pc-base-change]. Finiteness and radiciality are preserved by this scalar extension by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Therefore $\Phi$ is finite and radicial, with no separatedness or reducedness assumption.
